concepts.def: Elements arranged by atomic number into groups and periods.
Patterns in reactivity, e.g. Group 1 and Group 7.
Metals with variable oxidation states and coloured compounds.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Inorganic Chemistry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Inorganic Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Inorganic Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these Group 1 metals is the most reactive?
options: Potassium
Sodium
Lithium
They are all equally reactive

mcqs.q: When chlorine water is added to potassium bromide solution, the mixture:
options: Turns orange as bromine is displaced
Shows no change
Forms a white precipitate
Gives off hydrogen gas

mcqs.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper(II) sulfate solution?
options: Zinc
Silver
Gold
Copper
Salt + water + carbon dioxide
Salt + hydrogen
Salt + water only
Metal oxide + water

mcqs.q: Do Group 1 metals get less reactive down the group like the halogens?
options: Copper reacts with dilute acid to give off oxygen gas.
All Group 1 metals are equally reactive because each loses one electron.
Potassium is less reactive than lithium because bigger atoms are more stable.
No — Group 1 reactivity increases down the group because the outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily.

mcqs.q: Does copper fizz with dilute hydrochloric acid?
options: Nothing is oxidised or reduced in a displacement reaction.
No — copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from a dilute acid.
Copper reacts with dilute acid to give off oxygen gas.
All metals react with acid because metals are reactive substances.

mcqs.q: When chlorine displaces bromine from bromide solution, is the chlorine oxidised?
options: Copper reacts with dilute acid to give off oxygen gas.
No — each chlorine atom gains an electron to form chloride, so chlorine is reduced; the bromide ions are oxidised.
Chlorine is oxidised because it is the reactive one causing the reaction.
Nothing is oxidised or reduced in a displacement reaction.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Salt preparation”?
options: Dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of argon and carbon dioxide.
Acids release hydrogen ions in water and react with bases, metal carbonates and reactive metals to form salts.
An insoluble base is added to warm acid until in excess, the mixture filtered, and the salt crystallised from the solution.
Metals ranked by reactivity; a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its salt.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Group 1 alkali metals”?
options: Dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of argon and carbon dioxide.
Metals ranked by reactivity; a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its salt.
Lithium, sodium and potassium react with water to form hydroxides and hydrogen; reactivity increases down the group.
An insoluble base is added to warm acid until in excess, the mixture filtered, and the salt crystallised from the solution.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reactivity series”?
options: Acids release hydrogen ions in water and react with bases, metal carbonates and reactive metals to form salts.
Lithium, sodium and potassium react with water to form hydroxides and hydrogen; reactivity increases down the group.
Metals ranked by reactivity; a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its salt.
Dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of argon and carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Group 7 halogens”?
options: Lithium, sodium and potassium react with water to form hydroxides and hydrogen; reactivity increases down the group.
Reactivity decreases down the group; a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from a solution of its salt.
Metals ranked by reactivity; a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its salt.
Dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of argon and carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Composition of air”?
options: Acids release hydrogen ions in water and react with bases, metal carbonates and reactive metals to form salts.
Dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of argon and carbon dioxide.
Lithium, sodium and potassium react with water to form hydroxides and hydrogen; reactivity increases down the group.
Metals ranked by reactivity; a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its salt.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Acids and bases”?
options: Reactivity decreases down the group; a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from a solution of its salt.
Metals ranked by reactivity; a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its salt.
Lithium, sodium and potassium react with water to form hydroxides and hydrogen; reactivity increases down the group.
Acids release hydrogen ions in water and react with bases, metal carbonates and reactive metals to form salts.

mcqs.q: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. What volume of hydrogen at r.t.p. is produced from 0.50 mol of magnesium with excess acid? (1 mol of gas occupies 24 dm³)
options: 12 dm³
6 dm³
48 dm³
24 dm³

Orange liquid; displaces iodine from solution
Green gas; displaces bromine and iodine
